finding: The section map of the one-time migration (`read_section_map`, `section_target`, `rewrite_section_links`, and the link scanner behind them, about 340 lines) has no caller outside the tests. ST-0454 ran the rewrite once and added no command, so the code stays in the shared module `_link_rewrite.py` that `move-docs` and `migrate-spec-layout` import. The guard tests `test_handbook_links.py` re-run it on every test run. They read the work file `docs/spec/work/factory-handbooks-migration-map.md` and, through `git log --diff-filter=D`, the commit that deleted the guide. A later cleanup of `docs/spec/work/` or a shallow clone breaks or skips the guard, and a maintainer of `move-docs` must read the migration scanner to change the module. Fix: after the release, move the section-map code and its two test files out of `_link_rewrite.py` into a module that only the guard tests import, or delete both once `link-check` holds the same guarantee. Until then, name in the module header that the section map serves no command.
why_this_severity: The migration is done and its links resolve, so the feature meets its purpose (no to fails_purpose). The unused scanner and the coupling of the guard tests to a work file raise the cost of the next change to `_link_rewrite.py`. The code exists only on feature/handbooks.
